✨The science behind Manifestation? Your Reticular Activating System. 

Right now, your senses are taking in millions of pieces of information every second — sounds, sights, sensations. If you noticed all of it, you’d be paralysed. So your RAS filters almost everything out, and lets through only what it believes matters to you.

Here’s the powerful part: that filter isn’t fixed. It’s programmable.
When you set a goal with real clarity — and charge it with genuine emotion — you’re telling your RAS this matters now. And it begins showing you what it used to hide.

Tomorrow is 9.9
In numerology, 9 is the number of completion — of endings, of wisdom, of finally releasing what you have carried too long.

Here is what I invite you to do tomorrow:

✨ In the morning —
Sit quietly for 5 minutes. Ask yourself one question:
“What am I finally ready to let go of?”
Do not force an answer. Let it come.

✨ Through the day —
Every time you catch yourself replaying an old story — a fight, a fear, a version of yourself you have outgrown — pause. Take a breath. And gently say:
“I release you with love. You served me well. I am ready for what is next.”

✨ In the evening —
Write down what you are ready to complete. On paper. By hand.
Then quietly burn it, or tear it up. Not with anger. With gratitude.

✨ Before sleep —
Place your hand on your heart. Whisper to yourself:
“I am open to what is arriving.”

Save this. Share it with someone who needs it. And tomorrow, come tell me what you released. 🌸

With love,
Debalina

We mostly see the best polished parts of people’s lives.

Perfect routines.
Perfect skin.
Beautiful homes.
Aesthetic meals.
Always productive.
Always glowing.

After a point, it becomes easy to forget that real life usually looks much more ordinary than that.

There are also messy rooms,
off-track days,
simple routines,
unfinished tasks,
low-energy moments,
and phases where we are simply trying our best.

But when we constantly consume polished versions of other people’s lives, we sometimes start comparing them with our hardest days.

And slowly,
that comparison can affect our confidence,
self-worth,
and the way we see ourselves.

So I wanted to share a few real and unfiltered moments from my own life.

Not to romanticize imperfection.
Just to remind myself — and maybe someone else too —
that we are allowed to be human. 🤍

Why does Lord Jagannath’s form look so different? 

Perhaps because the Infinite was never meant to fit within human imagination. ✨

Jagat means the universe—everything that moves.
 Nātha means Lord and Master.
 Together, Jagannath means “The Lord of the Universe.”

His wide-open eyes symbolize awareness that never sleeps—witnessing everything without judgment.
His open arms remind us to welcome life while remaining free from attachment.

His unchanged smile represents the bliss that remains untouched by the changing world.

His undefined body and invisible feet remind us that the Divine cannot be limited by ordinary human form. Everything physical may change, but the consciousness within remains eternal.

Perhaps Lord Jagannath is not asking us to understand His appearance, but to awaken to the deeper truth it represents:
Can we observe without judging, love without possessing, act without attachment and remain peaceful through every change?

Jai Jagannath. 🕉️🙏

Rub your fingertips together for 10 seconds. Here’s what’s really happening in your brain. 🧠👇

Your fingertips are one of the most densely innervated areas of your entire body. 
Each fingertip packs in roughly 2,500 mechanoreceptors per square centimeter — Meissner’s corpuscles, Merkel cells, Pacinian and Ruffini endings — each tuned to a different quality of touch: light pressure, texture, vibration, stretch.

When you slow down and focus on that friction, you’re doing something specific: you’re activating your interoceptive and somatosensory networks and routing attention through the insular cortex, the brain region that maps internal bodily sensation.

And here’s the part that matters — when this network switches on, activity in your Default Mode Network quiets down. 

The DMN is the circuit responsible for mind-wandering, rumination, and that endless loop of self-referential thinking. 

You physically cannot be lost in overthinking and fully immersed in a present-moment sensation at the same time. The brain routes attention to one or the other.
This is the mechanism behind grounding techniques used in clinical settings for anxiety and stress regulation. It’s not “woo.” It’s applied attention science.
The sensation was always there. You just gave your brain permission to notice it.

This is exactly the kind of thing the Silva Method trains — deliberately shifting your mental state through awareness and attention, on demand.

You will struggle eating noodles with a spoon.

But nobody calls the fork useless.
Nobody calls the spoon unsuccessful.

Because we understand one simple thing:

Different tools have different purposes.

Someone is amazing at writing.
Someone is amazing at singing.
Someone loves a peaceful 9–5.
Someone feels alive building a business.
Someone grows fast.
Someone grows slowly.
Someone shines in public.
Someone blooms quietly.

And somehow we turn all of this into comparison.

“Am I behind?”
“Am I less talented?”

Maybe you’re not failing.
Maybe you’re just trying to use yourself in the wrong place.
Maybe you’re a fork trying to scoop soup.
Maybe you’re a spoon trying to fight with noodles.

Your purpose is not wrong.
Your pace is not wrong.
Your path is not wrong.

You just need to stop measuring your life with someone else’s design.

Some people are made for stages.
Some are made for pages.
Some are made for boardrooms.
Some are made for classrooms.
Some are made for art.
Some are made for strategy.
Some are made to build slowly, quietly, beautifully.

Different doesn’t mean less.
Different means designed differently.

So before you call yourself behind…

Am I actually failing?
Or am I trying to scoop soup with a fork?

Hear me out 💁🏻‍♀️

Many people want the same success.
Their actions tell different stories.

One breaks the climb into smaller steps and moves forward.
The other keeps attempting the same leap and stays stuck.

When a goal feels overwhelming, make the next action clearer:

→ Choose one task you keep avoiding.
→ Break it into three smaller actions.
→ Complete the first one today.

“Read more” becomes “read one page.”
“Finish the project” becomes “write the first paragraph.”

Give yourself a step you can actually take.

Save this for a day when starting feels difficult.
